Beyond his scientific contributions, Leakey also helped save Africa’s elephants and fight government corruption in his native Kenya. A swashbuckling, pugnacious real-life Indiana Jones, Leakey managed to cheat death many times—a childhood skull fracture, kidney and liver failures that required transplants, public beatings, and a plane crash—before passing away in his home outside Nairobi. Risk Factors for Pneumonia Feb. 25, 2026 Español Key points Pneumonia is an infection of the lungs. Pneumonia can cause mild to serious illness in people of all ages. Some people are at increased risk for getting pneumonia. Certain ages, health conditions, and behaviors can increase a person's risk for pneumonia. Talk to a healthcare provider if you have concerns about pneumonia. About risk There are many different germs that can cause pneumonia. The risk for pneumonia can be different for each cause. Keep Reading Causes People at increased risk People are more likely to get pneumonia at certain ages. For adults , those 65 years or older are at increased risk. Risk continues increasing as age increases: an 80-year-old has a higher risk than a 65-year-old adult. For children , those younger than 5 years old are at increased risk. Risk increases for children at younger ages: a 1-year-old has a higher risk than a 4-year-old child. Conditions that can increase risk People who have chronic (ongoing) medical conditions are at increased risk for pneumonia. These can include: Chronic heart disease Chronic liver disease Chronic lung disease

Risk Management for Existing Chemicals under TSCA The Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) gives EPA the authority to take action to address unreasonable risks to public health or the environment from chemicals currently on the market. If at the end of the risk evaluation process EPA determines that a chemical presents an unreasonable risk to health or the environment, the agency must immediately start the risk management process to reduce or eliminate these risks. Input from all stakeholders is critical to the risk management process. EPA is committed to developing risk management actions for chemicals in a way that is transparent and includes proactive, meaningful outreach and education with the public and other stakeholders. The mission of the program will be carried out by the Earthquake Engineering and Community Resilience groups via research on two thrust areas: (A) one focused on community resilience to natural and technological hazards, with objectives to enhance cost-effective local-level capacity to prepare, adapt, withstand, and recover from events; and (B) the second focused on earthquake risk reduction in buildings and infrastructure , with objectives to enhance the performance and recovery of the built environment from seismic hazards by advancing knowledge required to develop first-generation recovery-based design guides and standards, and to improve current performance-based design codes, in ways that enhance public safety, community resilience, and economic security. pages.text: Rivers and lakes are the most degraded ecosystems in the world. Can we save them? | National Geographic A kayaker on the Colorado River, Utah. Photograph by Ben Horton, Nat Geo Image Collection ENVIRONMENT NEWS Rivers and lakes are the most degraded ecosystems in the world. Can we save them? We rely on fresh water for drinking, food, and sanitation, and they’re in trouble. But freshwater issues are becoming a higher priority for conservationists. By Stefan Lovgren Published March 1, 2021 • 12 min read When Grand Canyon National Park was established a century ago, the Colorado River running through it was treated as an afterthought. In the decades following, states scrambled to squeeze every drop of water out of the Colorado for farming and drinking, with a cascade of huge dams constructed along its course. Native fish like suckers and chubs, found nowhere else in the world, were replaced with invasive catfish and bass that were more attractive for anglers. In time, the mighty river that had once carved out one of America’s most iconic landscapes was reduced to a trickle, no longer able to fulfill its destiny of reaching the sea. What happened to the Colorado is a powerful example of a river’s decline, but it’s hardly an exception. Around the world, rivers, lakes, and wetlands have increasingly come under similar assault from poorly planned dams, pollution, habitat loss, sand mining, climate change, and the introduction of invasive species. George Washington was sent to deter French troops from challenging the British for control of the strategic Forks of the Ohio. The action had far-reaching consequences for Washington, transforming him from an inexperienced soldier into a battle-hardened leader. Washington led 159 Virginia militiamen over the Appalachian Mountains and built a rough military road as far as western Pennsylvania. There he joined forces with a Seneca chief named Tanaghrisson, a pivotal figure whose loyalty to the British proved critical. Together, they surprised and routed a small party of French troops, killing a dozen of them and their commander. Anticipating retaliation, Washington’s men hurriedly built Fort Necessity, where they were attacked in July by the French and their Indigenous allies. Gen. Bolen is the inventor of Button Helper, a patented dressing aid for individuals of differing physical and intellectual abilities. He secured adoption of the assistive device by the Defense Health Agency and Veterans Health Administration, then drove commercialization across international clinical and retail channels. Robin Hilton Host and Senior Producer of Tiny Desk and All Songs Considered Robin Hilton is a host and senior producer for the All Songs Considered podcast and Tiny Desk, a series he helped create — and named — in 2008. He's since produced performances at the Desk by Harry Styles, Chance The Rapper, Alana Springsteen, Steve Martin, and more. Hilton got his first full-time job as a reporter at a member station when he was 19 years old. He went on to win more than two dozen awards for his work, as both a reporter and a newscaster, from The AP, the National Association Of Broadcasters, Public Media Journalists Association (then called PRNDI) and more. He eventually landed at Morning Edition , where he worked as a Production Assistant before starting as the Assistant Producer for All Songs Considered in 2001. Along with Bob Boilen, Hilton helped turn All Songs Considered into one of the most popular and influential music programs in the country, officially becoming the co-host in 2008 and, after Boilen's retirement in 2023, the permanent host. He is also a composer whose music has appeared in films, podcasts and radio, including his arrangement of NPR's Weekend All Things Considered theme and NPR's Elections theme. Despite assistance from the US Navy, ships are still being attacked . "To transit the Strait of Hormuz you need agreement between the captain and the crew to take the risk. You need war risk insurance. And the captain has to make the final decision," says Steve Cameron, a former merchant navy officer and maritime consultant. Missiles and drones are a threat from the air, but under the surface mines may also be lurking. "If you're a captain, you'd like to see evidence mines aren't present," Cameron adds. Modern mines rest on the seabed and detonate when they detect an acoustic or magnetic signal, triggering a pressure wave that will break the keel of a passing vessel. Others can rise through shallow waters or float, or be powered towards a target. The technology itself is not difficult or costly, but the mere threat can stop a tanker fleet from sailing. pages.text: Ronaldo, Maradona, Baggio - what happened to the World XI? - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images By Alex Bysouth BBC Sport senior journalist Published 17 November 2026, 07:22 GMT Soren Colding wasn't expecting the call. "The Laudrup brothers, Peter Schmeichel, there might have been some cancellations," he jokes. Eventually, the Danish FA turned to a Brondby defender who had played a handful of times for the national team. The assignment? He would be expected to mark Ronaldo and Gabriel Batistuta as part of a Europe XI against the Rest of the World at Marseille's Velodrome. It was December 1997, and Colding's team-mates would include defenders Fernando Hierro and Alessandro Costacurta, a midfield duo of Zinedine Zidane and Paul Ince, and Patrick Kluivert and Alen Boksic up top. This was a star-sprinkled cast - one player from each of the competing nations at the following summer's World Cup joining forces before the draw took place. "Of course, when you see those names, it was just more or less a dream come true," explains the Dane. Colding was flown to France and chauffeured to the hotel. His driver offered to hang around in case the full-back fancied an impromptu shopping trip. There was no need. Instead, he discovered a bag of Fifa goodies in his room. "There was the biggest Adidas bag I have ever seen in my life," he smiles. "I found a training suit and went down to lunch. "Then I saw all the other guys on round tables - they were sitting with their agents, their wives, their family, their friends in normal [clothes]. Then the Danish guy turned in. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Rose Guano Cave Important Stop for Migrating Bats on BLM-Managed Public Lands in Nevada Oct 26, 2026 A bat in Rose Guano Cave in Nevada. (Photo courtesy of Joseph Danielson/Nevada Department of Wildlife) Tucked within eastern Nevada public lands is a haven for bats: Rose Guano Cave. Nestled in the remote landscape of White Pine County, Rose Guano Cave serves as critical habitat for one of the largest concentrations of bats in the region and provides an important stopover during migration from July through October each year. The number of bats using Rose Guano Cave fluctuates annually, with population estimates typically ranging between 1 and 3 million bats. Bats fly from Rose Guano Cave in Nevada. pages.text: RSS Feed (Really Simple Syndication) - BBC Sport Published 22 May 2024 What is RSS? In a world heaving under the weight of billions of web pages, keeping up to date with the information you want can be a drag. Wouldn't it be better to have the latest news and features delivered directly to you, rather than clicking from site to site? Using RSS (Really Simple Syndication) allows you to see when sites from all over the internet have added new content. You can get the latest headlines and articles (or even audio files, photographs or video) in one place, as soon as they are published, without having to remember to visit each site every day. RSS takes the hassle out of staying up-to-date, by showing you the very latest information that you are interested in. RSS feeds are just a special kind of web page, designed to be read by computers rather than people. It might help to think of them as the free, internet version of the old-fashioned ticker-tape news wire machines. Not all websites currently provide RSS and not all sections of the BBC or BBC Sport website are available as feeds. How do I start using RSS feeds? Close Rub21's Diary A map of open OSM notes, sorted by what they need Posted by Rub21 on 12 November 2026 in English . There are about 450,000 open notes on OpenStreetMap. Each one is a message from someone who saw a problem on the map. But to know what a note needs, you have to open it and read it, one by one. That takes a lot of time. So I trained a machine learning model to do this first read for us. I also made a simple website to show the results: → https://osm-notes.rub21.com What does the model do? The model reads the first comment of each note and gives it two labels: Category : what the mapper should do. For example: missing place, place closed or changed, wrong name, missing or wrong road, other wrong data, spam, empty, or not mappable (opinions, questions). Theme : what the note is about. For example: food, shops, health, roads, transport. How I built it The notes. Andrés ( AngocA ) built OSM-Notes-Ingestion . It loads all OSM notes into a database and keeps them up to date every minute. The data team at Mapbox have built tools that allow detecting and cleaning these issues as they happen on the map. Detecting issues with OSMlint To detect issues, we run spatial analysis on the map data of the whole world everyday using OSMlint . This is made possible be leveraging the power of tile-reduce to analyze OpenStreetMap vector tiles using javascript. OSMlint consists of a set of validators which check the data on each tile for common issues in geometry and tags. An example validator is crossingHighways which detects roads that cross each other without an intersection. Each validator produces a GeoJSON output of the OpenStreetMap geometries that are invalid and needs review. Fixing issues with To-fix To-fix is a micro tasking tool that helps us create tasks of issues to fix on OpenStreetMap. The issues collected with OSMlint is loaded into to-fix, each of which is then reviewed by a member of the mapping community or the Mapbox data team. Over 500,000 issues have been fixed so far using to-fix. To-fix also allows marking issues as false positives. These are later investigated and used to improve the validator algorithm in OSMlint. The linting pipeline We’ve implemented an architecture that automates the detection of issues using OSMlint and loading them into to-fix on a daily basis. pages.text: Russell Brand prison message claiming innocence being investigated, No 10 says Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Russell Brand prison message 'appalling' and being investigated, No 10 says 45 minutes ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Sima Kotecha Senior UK correspondent Reuters Russell Brand (pictured during his trial) delivered a message to followers via his wife Laura A message by Russell Brand to his followers in which he claimed innocence for his sexual offences was "clearly appalling" and is being urgently investigated, Downing Street has said. The comedian is currently serving a 10-and-half-year prison sentence after being convicted of rape and three counts of sexual assault. His wife Laura read out a message from him on their Sunday Service show on YouTube, in which the convicted rapist claimed: "I am not guilty of the offences I have been jailed for." No 10 said it expects action to be taken if Brand is found to have broken prison rules. Justice Secretary Alex Norris said the broadcast of a statement from Russell Brand is "completely unacceptable". In a post on X, Norris wrote: "Prisoners are rightly banned from making statements that cause distress to victims. "This is being urgently investigated, and I expect action to be taken if he is found to have broken the rules." pages.text: Russia barred from Junior Ice Hockey World Championships in Canada - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022 By Dan Roan Sports editor Published 15 November 2026 Russia's hopes of reintegration into international sport suffered a setback when it was barred from the upcoming Junior Ice Hockey World Championships in Canada. It comes despite a ruling by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) last month ordering the country's return to the competition. The hosts then said they would deny entry to Russian athletes as a result of the war in Ukraine. "Due to the position and restrictions formally communicated by the Canadian government, the Russian Under-20 national team is unable to participate in the World Junior Championship," the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) said in a statement. It added that "after carefully assessing the feasibility of alternative arrangements, the IIHF Council has determined that Canada will remain as host and the tournament will proceed from 26 December 2026 to 5 January 2027 in Edmonton and Red Deer." The Russian Ice Hockey Federation called the IIHF's decision "unacceptable and unlawful" and said it would appeal to the International Olympic Committee (IOC). "The IIHF's decision was made solely due to political reasons," it added. "The exclusion of the Russian national team violates fundamental legal principles, Olympism, the principle of non-discrimination, equality among athletes and the integrity of international tournaments." More than three dozen of them sat huddled along a wall, wearing face masks because of the Covid pandemic. One Russian newspaper reporter described them as "pale and sleep-deprived". On entering, Putin sat down at the opposite side of the hall, creating a vast space between him and the businessmen. As usual, he was wearing no mask. Using his typically coded language, he said he expected them to support the war. "I would like to call on you to show understanding of what is going on," he said, "and work together with the government to find the tools which would support production, the economy, jobs." In the Kremlin-published video of the meeting, none of the invited billionaires said a word. That silence has become a feature of the Russian super-rich. Russia tops the list of global exporters of fossil fuels, with its vast coal, oil and gas deposits. Saudi Arabia, one of the world’s biggest producers of oil and gas, comes next with about 60 gigatonnes of CO 2 exported. pages.text: Ryan Crowley: Airman's rugby career has taken off at Leicester Tigers - BBC Sport Image source, Shutterstock Image caption, Ryan Crowley has scored two tries in 10 matches for Leicester Tigers By Andrew Aloia BBC Sport, East Midlands Published 18 November 2026 Corporal Ryan Crowley has spent a decade helping get aircraft off the ground. It has taken just as long for the winger to finally get his professional rugby union career to take off. It was only a year ago that Crowley was plucked from his role as an avionics engineer with the Royal Air Force and recruited by Leicester Tigers. The 28-year-old Welshman was handed a deal with the giants of the game, the 11-time Prem champions - when he didn't even know one was up for grabs. "I thought I got sent up to Tigers to go and get experience and do a pre-season with a pro team," he told BBC Sport. The military man had simply followed orders. Chinnor, the second division side he was playing for, asked him to join Geoff Parling's Tigers for the early weeks of their Prem Rugby Cup campaign last season. "After a couple of weeks Geoff said, 'you've been successful in your trial', and I was like, 'what trial?'," Crowley added. "The silver lining to not knowing it was a trial is I had no pressure on me; I just came up and I was just trying to learn as much as I could. "I didn't have any expectations of having to come out the end of it with something, but luckily I did." He focuses on the national security side of the Justice beat, including counterterrorism, counterintelligence and transnational repression. Before joining NPR, Lucas worked for a decade as a foreign correspondent for The Associated Press based in Poland, Egypt and Lebanon. In Poland, he covered the fallout from the revelations about secret CIA prisons in Eastern Europe. In the Middle East, he reported on the ouster of Hosni Mubarak in 2011 and the turmoil that followed. He also covered the Libyan civil war, the Syrian conflict and the rise of the Islamic State. He reported from Iraq during the U.S. occupation and later during the Islamic State takeover of Mosul in 2014. He also covered intelligence and national security for Congressional Quarterly. Lucas earned a bachelor's degree from The College of William and Mary, and a master's degree from Jagiellonian University in Krakow, Poland. That said, planning is an important step in being prepared and ready for your adventure. Remember, the Monument can be very unforgiving, and its wild character should not be underestimated. And although overnight stays on the monument do not require a permit, free permits are available at any of the local Visitor Centers and are highly encouraged. The permit system can become crucial in the case of a search and rescue . Below are some best practices to keep in mind when recreating on the GSENM: It’s always a good idea to let people know your itinerary and when you expect be back Travel in groups rather than by yourself Before beginning any of your Monument adventures, make sure you've planned your way in, and planned your way out Know the extended weather forecast Carry extra clothing, blankets, food and water for emergencies Remember, cell phone coverage across the Monument is sparse if at all Plan Ahead and Prepare
